quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Drive close behind the car in front of you.
Pass the car in front of you as quickly as possible.
Do not tailgate and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not tailgate and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: In work zones, stay far away from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other cars. Leave more space between your vehicle and the one in front of you.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross in front of you. What should you do before turning?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait until the person crosses the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the person crosses the street.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes have the right-of-way at all times. You must let them cross before you proceed.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Four lanes of traffic ahead.
A divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that you are leaving a one-way highway and entering a two-way highway where traffic comes from both directions.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may turn in the direction of the arrow if you:

options.text: Come to a complete stop first.
Wait until the light changes.
Are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear of traffic.
questions.explanation: You may turn in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the right lane and no pedestrians or vehicles are in the intersection. Always yield to anyone already in the intersection.

questions.question: This symbol is used for:

options.text: Dangerous intersections.
Slow-moving vehicles.
Yield signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: An orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it moves slowly. You may see this on farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. It looks orange during the day and red at night.

questions.question: Vehicles stopped behind a school bus with red lights flashing must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students get off the bus.
The stop arm is pulled in.
The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving again.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving again.
questions.explanation: When a school bus flashes red lights and extends its stop arm, you must stay stopped until the lights turn off, the arm is pulled in, and the bus moves again.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means doing anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is the leading cause of crashes. Any distraction can cause you to miss important sights and sounds that could prevent an accident.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No turns allowed.
No outlet.
No U-turns allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that U-turns are not permitted. You often see this sign at intersections where oncoming traffic is heavy.

questions.question: To see vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Look in your inside rearview mirror.
Look in your outside rearview mirror.
Turn and look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn and look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. The only way to see them is to turn your head and look over your shoulders.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line is next to a broken yellow line, passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line. Passing is not allowed from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: Which of the following blocks traffic flow?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: An oncoming vehicle is approaching while you want to pass a pedestrian walking on the road. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to get the pedestrian to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. If you want to pass a pedestrian but an oncoming vehicle is coming, slow down and let it pass. Then you can pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: A sign with this shape means:

options.text: No passing zone.
Right turn allowed on red.
Yield right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign marks the start of a no passing zone.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows there is a pedestrian crosswalk.

questions.question: If you park your car in an unusual spot, what should you do?

options.text: Park with your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your car from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your car from all directions.
questions.explanation: Your parked car must not become a hazard. Make sure your car is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Any prescription drug is safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
Only illegal drugs can affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving ability, including cold medicine, allergy medicine, and calming drugs. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of any drug that impairs driving, whether it is illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A downward-facing triangle sign is always a yield sign. Be ready to slow down or stop when you see it.

questions.question: Before starting the engine, you should:

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers buckle their safety belts.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Create a habit for getting in and out of your car. Before starting the engine, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, it is hard to see and be seen. How can you let other drivers know you are there?

options.text: Turn up the dashboard lights.
Turn on your parking lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you cannot see other vehicles or when other drivers cannot see you. Always use low beam headlights when weather requires you to use windshield wipers.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Sharp turn to the right ahead.
Sharp left and right turns ahead.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a winding road ahead. Adjust your speed accordingly.

questions.question: Which of these substances can make it unsafe to drive?

options.text: Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. These include tranquilizers, sedatives, over-the-counter cough and cold medicines, allergy medications, and illegal drugs. Some of these contain alcohol, codeine, or antihistamines that affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: When you see this yellow sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop at the crosswalk.
Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard signals you to go.
Be ready to stop if children are crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are crossing.
questions.explanation: This five-sided sign means you are near a school. Stay alert and be ready to stop if you see children in the crosswalk.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Be ready for anything.
Expect construction workers to let you through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected changes and hazards. Drive with extra caution to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Assume the child has full control of the bicycle.
Be ready for anything.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable and may suddenly change direction. Children and bicycles are small and hard to see. Always stay alert around them.

questions.question: If you need your lights on while driving due to weather or darkness:

options.text: Use your parking lights.
Use your high beams.
Use your low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect back off these conditions and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: No one can pass in either direction.
Everyone can pass in both directions.
Only drivers next to the dashed line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only drivers next to the dashed line can pass.
questions.explanation: When a dashed yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, only the traffic beside the dashed line may cross the center to pass. Drivers beside the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: The driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Pass carefully at 10 mph or slower.
Stop and wait for all pedestrians to finish crossing.
Change lanes, look, and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for all pedestrians to finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. Pedestrians may be crossing where you cannot see them. Stop and wait until all pedestrians have fully crossed.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns of a steep hill. Slow down to avoid crashes and brake damage.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They create vibration and sound to alert drivers who have drifted out of their lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: They create vibration and sound to alert drivers who have drifted out of their lane.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips make noise and vibrations to warn drowsy or distracted drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic signal.

questions.question: This sign indicates:

options.text: The space from the road to a bridge or overpass.
The maximum legal vehicle height in this state.
The maximum width of a vehicle allowed on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The space from the road to a bridge or overpass.
questions.explanation: This is a low clearance warning sign. It shows the distance from the road surface to the bottom of a bridge or overpass (in this case, 12 feet 6 inches).
